hero.headline: Meteor explodes off Massachusetts coast, causing sonic boom across New England
hero.body:
A meteor exploded over the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Massachusetts, creating a sonic boom heard across Southern New England. Reports of the loud noise and sightings of the meteor came from areas stretching from Delaware to Montreal.

The Boston Herald reported that authorities identified the mysterious noise as a sonic boom, possibly caused by a meteor that exploded in mid-air. CBS News confirmed the meteor detonated off the Massachusetts coast, generating the loud boom that alarmed residents throughout the region.

According to the Worcester Telegram, the explosion released energy equivalent to 300 tons of TNT. The meteor disintegrated over the ocean rather than reaching the ground, which likely prevented any damage or injuries.

Sonic booms from meteors occur when the space rock travels through the atmosphere faster than the speed of sound, creating a shock wave. When meteors explode in mid-air, the sudden release of energy amplifies the sound, making it audible over wide areas.

Residents across Southern New England reported hearing the boom and took to social media to share their experiences. The widespread reports helped authorities piece together what had occurred and rule out other potential causes for the noise.

The event took place over the Atlantic Ocean, away from populated areas. No injuries or property damage were reported following the explosion. Meteors entering Earth's atmosphere are relatively common, though most burn up at high altitudes without creating noticeable effects on the ground.

The sightings and reports spanned a large geographic area, indicating the meteor was visible from multiple states and into Canada. The explosion occurred at an altitude high enough that the sonic boom could travel across the region but low enough to be clearly heard by people on the ground.

cards.headline: U.S. military disables commercial ship attempting to breach Iran blockade
cards.body:
The U.S. military attacked and seized an Iranian-flagged container ship that tried to pass through an American blockade near the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first such interception since the blockade began last week.

U.S. Central Command said marines from the USS Tripoli assault ship rappelled onto the vessel, called the Touska, by helicopter on Sunday. President Trump announced the action on social media, saying a U.S. Navy guided missile destroyer had warned the Touska to stop in the Gulf of Oman, but the ship refused to comply. "Our Navy ship stopped them right in their tracks by blowing a hole in the engine room," Trump said. He noted that U.S. marines now had custody of the vessel.

Video released by the U.S. Defense Department showed the USS Spruance firing on the Touska. Audio from the interception captured a U.S. sailor telling the crew to vacate the engine room, warning that disabling fire would follow if they did not comply. The ship had previously departed Port Klang in Malaysia before attempting to breach the blockade near Iran's border with Pakistan.

Trump said the ship was under U.S. Treasury sanctions due to prior illegal activity and appeared on the Treasury Department's list of sanctioned vessels.

Iran's joint military command rejected the seizure, calling it an act of piracy that violated a ceasefire in place since April 8. A spokesperson for Iran's military said the armed forces would "soon respond and retaliate against this armed piracy." Iranian state media reported that Tehran had rejected new peace talks, citing the ongoing blockade, threatening rhetoric, and what officials described as excessive U.S. demands and shifting positions.

The incident throws uncertainty over planned negotiations. Trump had announced that U.S. negotiators would travel to Pakistan on Monday for another round of talks with Iran, but Iran has not confirmed its attendance. The ceasefire is scheduled to expire Wednesday.

The confrontation threatens to deepen the global energy crisis and push the two countries toward renewed conflict. The war has killed at least 3,000 people in Iran, nearly 2,300 in Lebanon, 23 civilians and 15 soldiers in Israel, and more than a dozen in Gulf Arab states. Thirteen U.S. service members have also been killed.

The blockade of Iranian ports has been central to U.S. military operations during the conflict. The seizure of the Touska demonstrates the continued military enforcement of the blockade even as diplomatic efforts continue, reflecting the dual approach of maintaining military pressure while pursuing negotiations.

cards.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks in next 48 hours
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch a major attack within the next two days based on intelligence from US and European allies.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is bracing for a major attack from Russia expected within the next 48 hours, based on intelligence shared by the U.S. and European allies. He anticipates the attacks will occur at night in the coming days.

The Ukrainian government is preparing for what it expects will be significant military action from Russian forces.

cards.headline: 11 workers killed in Washington paper mill chemical explosion, all bodies recovered
cards.teaser: Officials recovered and identified all victims from the Nippon mill tank implosion in Longview.
cards.body:
All 11 workers killed in a chemical explosion at a Longview, Washington paper mill have been recovered and identified, according to local officials. The victims died in a tank implosion at the Nippon mill facility.

Authorities have released the names of all workers who died in the incident. The recovery effort concluded after officials located all missing victims from the disaster site. The explosion occurred at the paper mill's chemical processing area.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo claims over 245 lives
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed 65 people, with health officials reporting 246 suspected cases so far. The outbreak is concentrated in Ituri province, a conflict-affected region that borders Uganda and South Sudan.

The strain identified in this outbreak is the Bundibugyo variant, according to DRC health officials. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention said the DRC's national research laboratory detected the Ebola virus in 13 of 20 samples tested. This strain is particularly concerning because no licensed vaccine currently exists for it, unlike the Zaire strain that has caused most previous Ebola outbreaks in the DRC. The Bundibugyo strain has appeared only twice before, in 2007 and 2012.

Uganda has also confirmed cases linked to the outbreak. A 59-year-old man died in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC, marking Uganda's first confirmed death from the current outbreak.

The World Health Organization estimates the death rate from confirmed cases at between 30 and 50 percent. Anaïs Legand, from the WHO's high threat pathogens team, described this as significant, noting that up to five out of ten infected people are likely to die. The head of the WHO has visited the region to support containment efforts.

Ituri province presents particular challenges for disease control. The region contains mining towns with constant population movement, making it difficult to track and contain the spread of infectious disease. The vast geography of the DRC and ongoing security challenges in some areas further complicate surveillance and response efforts.

Health workers in the affected areas face significant obstacles. Medical facilities lack sufficient resources to manage the increasing number of cases, and workers struggle to access remote communities. Maintaining the cold chain required for vaccines and treatments adds another layer of difficulty in this region.

The medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières described the situation as deeply alarming, highlighting the strain on local health systems. Aid organizations are working to support underequipped health workers as they respond to the outbreak.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention convened an urgent meeting with authorities from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan, along with the WHO and pharmaceutical companies. Dr Jean Kaseya, the director general of Africa CDC, emphasized the need for rapid regional coordination given the high population movement between affected areas and neighboring countries.

The DRC has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976. Cases in the current outbreak have been reported mainly in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with suspected cases also appearing in the neighboring city of Bunia.

cards.headline: UN blacklists Israeli and Russian forces for sexual violence during conflict
cards.teaser: The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces to its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict, including allegations of rape against detained Palestinians.
cards.body:
The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces for the first time to its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict. The inclusion covers allegations of rape against detained Palestinians by Israeli forces.

The report released lists 77 government and non-government parties in countries credibly suspected of patterns of rape or other forms of sexual violence during armed conflict. This marks the first time either Israeli or Russian forces have appeared on the list.

cards.headline: Drone crashes into Romanian apartment building as war spills across border
cards.teaser: A drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war into civilian homes.
cards.body:
Residents of an apartment building in eastern Romania were jolted awake early Friday morning when a drone crashed into their home, causing a loud explosion and fire. The incident sent panic through the building as people fled to safety.

The crash underscored the precarious situation facing Romanians living near the Ukrainian border during the Russia-Ukraine war. As residents began returning to assess the damage to their homes, many expressed fear about their safety, with some saying they no longer feel secure in their own communities.

cards.headline: Four more miners rescued from flooded Laos cave after 10 days
cards.teaser: Rescue teams freed four additional people from a flooded cave in Laos where miners have been trapped for over a week.
cards.body:
Four more men have been freed from a flooded cave in Laos following a hazardous rescue operation. The miners were among seven villagers who entered the narrow tunnels on 20 May to search for gold. The first person was rescued on Friday, with four more freed in subsequent operations.

Two people remain missing as rescue teams continue navigating through muddy water, sharp rocks, and narrow passages. Divers have been working to drain water from the cave and manage collapse hazards as they search deeper into the system.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested after PSG Champions League victory sparks unrest in France
cards.teaser: Police arrested hundreds of people after celebrations of Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League win over Arsenal turned into disorder.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory over Arsenal ignited wild celebrations in France that descended into disorder. Thousands of police officers were deployed to manage unrest as crowds of fans took to the streets. Some celebrants fired flares during the festivities.

Law enforcement worked to quell the disturbances as they spread through areas where fans had gathered. Hundreds of people were arrested during the unrest.

cards.headline: Edgar Morin, French philosopher and former Resistance member, dies at 104
cards.teaser: Edgar Morin, a philosopher whose books and pronouncements carried moral authority across eras and disciplines, has died at 104.
cards.body:
Edgar Morin, a towering figure among French intellectuals, has died at age 104. A former member of the Resistance during World War II, Morin went on to a career that spanned multiple eras and academic disciplines.

His books and public pronouncements carried significant moral authority in France and beyond. Morin's work crossed traditional academic boundaries, addressing topics ranging from sociology to philosophy to political thought throughout his long career.

cards.headline: Colombia votes as leftist candidate faces far-right challenger in presidential race
cards.teaser: Colombians head to the polls with a leftist candidate leading but facing a far-right outsider who has gained momentum.
cards.body:
Colombia holds presidential elections that represent a crucial test for the left in Latin America. The leftist candidate leads in polls but faces a strengthening challenge from a far-right outsider who calls himself The Tiger.

The far-right candidate has gained momentum in the final stretch of the campaign. The election outcome will have significant implications for the direction of leftist movements across Latin America, with observers watching closely to see whether the region's recent leftward shift continues or faces a reversal.

cards.headline: Ecuador accused of interfering in Colombian election with tariff offer
cards.teaser: Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing Colombian presidential candidate before the vote.
cards.body:
Ecuador's President Daniel Noboa has offered to cancel tariffs following a conversation with a right-wing Colombian presidential candidate, drawing accusations of election meddling. The pledge comes days before Colombia's presidential election on Sunday.

The timing of Noboa's public commitment to reverse trade policy raises concerns about electoral interference. The offer, made contingent on the candidate's political success, potentially violates international norms governing electoral conduct and foreign involvement in sovereign elections.

cards.headline: Trump administration revises green card policy after initial announcement
cards.teaser: The Department of Homeland Security said most immigrants will not need to leave the U.S. to obtain green cards.
cards.body:
The Department of Homeland Security clarified that most immigrants will not be required to leave the United States to obtain green cards, backing away from earlier messaging. The reversal came after the initial policy announcement prompted widespread confusion and anxiety.

The Trump administration's initial green card policy changes had suggested applicants would need to depart the country during the application process. DHS officials have now downplayed the impact of the changes, stating the requirement will affect fewer people than initially understood.

cards.headline: Five killed in Virginia bus crash, including family traveling to wedding
cards.teaser: A family of four heading to a wedding died in the Interstate 95 collision that sent 44 others to hospitals.
cards.body:
Five people died in a bus crash in Stafford County, Virginia, including a family of four traveling to a family wedding. The collision on Interstate 95 sent 44 additional people to hospitals.

The bus driver has been charged in connection with the crash. The National Transportation Safety Board said a high rate of speed factored into the collision. The investigation into the crash continues.

cards.headline: ICE agent charged in Minnesota shooting arrested in Texas
cards.teaser: The agent faces charges related to the shooting of a Venezuelan man during an immigration raid in Minneapolis.
cards.body:
An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent charged in connection with a shooting in north Minneapolis has been arrested in Texas. The agent faces charges for shooting a Venezuelan man during an immigration raid in January.

The shooting occurred during Operation Metro Surge, an immigration enforcement operation. The agent was taken into custody in Texas after charges were filed related to the Minneapolis incident.

cards.headline: Meteor explodes off Massachusetts coast, causing loud boom across New England
cards.teaser: The explosion was equivalent to 300 tons of TNT and was reported from Delaware to Montreal.
cards.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT. The fireball broke apart at an altitude of 40 miles while traveling at 75,000 miles per hour, according to NASA.

The explosion triggered loud booms that echoed across the northeastern United States, with reports of the noise coming from a wide area including Delaware and Montreal.

hero.headline: United Airlines Flight Diverted After Passenger Attempts to Breach Cockpit
hero.teaser: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison after a passenger allegedly attempted to access the cockpit mid-flight.
hero.body:
United Airlines flight 2005, heading from Chicago to Minneapolis, diverted to Madison, Wisconsin after a passenger became unruly and attempted to breach the cockpit. The crew issued a hijacking alert in response to the incident. The passenger was arrested after the aircraft landed.

Multiple passengers witnessed the disturbance during the flight. The FBI was involved in the investigation following the emergency landing.

cards.headline: SoftBank Commits Up to $75 Billion to Build AI Data Centers in France
cards.teaser: SoftBank announced plans to invest up to $75 billion in French artificial intelligence facilities in what would be Europe's largest AI infrastructure project.
cards.body:
SoftBank pledged to invest up to €75 billion to build AI data centers in France, representing Europe's largest such investment. The Japanese conglomerate plans to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity through the project.

The facility will become Europe's biggest AI infrastructure complex, positioning France as a major hub for artificial intelligence computing resources in the region.

cards.headline: New Car Sales Drop as One Million Buyers Exit US Market
cards.teaser: The American new car market has lost approximately one million buyers as sales decline for the eighth consecutive month.
cards.body:
Auto sales in the United States have fallen for eight straight months, with roughly one million new car buyers disappearing from the market. The decline affects the overall automotive industry as fewer Americans purchase new vehicles.

Electric vehicle demand has collapsed as part of the broader sales downturn. Drivers face financial pressures that have made new car purchases increasingly difficult. Despite stagnating sales volumes, automakers continue to report profits according to industry data.

cards.headline: Ferrari Faces Criticism Over First Electric Vehicle Design
cards.teaser: Ferrari's debut electric vehicle, the Luce, has drawn backlash from critics who say the design departs from the brand's traditional identity.
cards.body:
The Luce, Ferrari's first electric vehicle intended to compete with Chinese EV manufacturers, has generated significant criticism since its unveiling. The Italian luxury automaker's entry into the electric vehicle market represents a major strategic shift for the brand.

Critics have accused Ferrari of abandoning its core identity with the new electric model. The backlash centers on the vehicle's design and the brand's pivot toward electrification in response to competition from Chinese EV makers.

cards.headline: China's Drug Development Industry Gains Attention at International Oncology Conference
cards.teaser: Clinical trials conducted in China are drawing focus at a major oncology gathering in Chicago as the country's biotechnology sector expands rapidly.
cards.body:
Clinical trials from China drew significant attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago. This visibility underscores the country's growing involvement in global drug development.

China's expanding biotechnology sector is reshaping the competitive landscape of pharmaceutical innovation. The country's rising prominence in clinical research has prompted concerns about the future of U.S. leadership in drug development globally.

cards.headline: Startups Offer Free Cleaning Services in Exchange for Recording Household Chores
cards.teaser: Technology companies are paying people to film themselves doing household tasks to help train artificial intelligence systems.
cards.body:
A startup is offering to clean apartments for free if residents allow the work to be recorded for AI training purposes. The recordings capture cleaning activities and household chores to develop machine learning models.

Multiple technology companies are pursuing similar programs, seeking video data of people performing everyday tasks like washing dishes and organizing clutter. Workers are being compensated to record themselves doing routine household work as tech firms gather training data for AI systems.

cards.headline: Sound Transit Shelves Ballard Light Rail Extension in Seattle
cards.teaser: Sound Transit approved a major update to its expansion plans, putting the Ballard light rail line on hold amid affordability concerns.
cards.body:
The Sound Transit Board approved significant changes to its ST3 project plans, leaving the Ballard light rail extension in limbo. The transit agency cited affordability issues as the reason for shelving portions of the planned light rail expansion.

Seattle residents and officials are questioning whether refunds will be provided after the Ballard line was postponed. The Seattle City Council indicated it would continue advocating for the Ball

cards.headline: Nvidia-powered Windows PCs to debut next week
cards.teaser: The first Windows computers using Nvidia processors will be unveiled at an upcoming event.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm have posted cryptic messages on social media ahead of the GTC event, where the first Windows PCs powered by Nvidia chips are expected to debut. According to Axios, these new computers will feature Nvidia's N1X laptop processors.

The Verge reported that all three companies are teasing the new processors ahead of the launch. PCMag noted the cryptic announcements have raised questions about whether Arm-powered Windows PC chips are finally arriving in the consumer market.

cards.headline: Blue moon visible tonight
cards.teaser: The second full moon of May appears in the night sky.
cards.body:
A blue moon is set to appear in UK skies tonight. Despite its name, the moon won't actually turn blue. The term "blue moon" refers to the second full moon occurring within a single calendar month—a relatively rare astronomical event.

Tonight offers a good opportunity to view the phenomenon, with clear skies expected and the bright moon easily visible. Observers in the UK can look up this evening to witness the event.

cards.headline: SoftBank to invest up to $75 billion in French data centers
cards.teaser: The investment aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion in French data centers. The company aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity throughout the country.

This investment underscores the growing demand for cloud computing and data processing infrastructure in France, as businesses increasingly rely on robust digital services.

cards.headline: Newly discovered fungus may help restore British habitats damaged by invasive moss
cards.teaser: A killer fungus species raises hope for restoring native habitats.
cards.body:
A newly discovered fungus species could help restore British habitats that have been damaged by invasive moss. The fungus targets the invasive plant species, offering a potential biological control method.

Researchers believe the discovery raises hope that some native British habitats could be restored to their original state. The fungus appears to specifically attack the invasive moss without harming native plant species.

cards.headline: GitHub Copilot switches to token-based billing
cards.teaser: The new billing model has sparked criticism among developers.
cards.body:
Microsoft's GitHub Copilot introduced a new token-based billing system that has generated criticism from developers. The change marks a shift in how the AI coding assistant charges for its services.

Developers have expressed concern about the new pricing structure. The token-based model replaces the previous billing approach, leading some to suggest the golden age of GitHub Copilot has ended.

cards.headline: Former Snap employees launch Ghost Angels fund
cards.teaser: Twenty Snap alumni created a fund to invest in the next generation of social media.
cards.body:
Twenty Snap alumni have joined forces to establish Ghost Angels, a new investment fund dedicated to backing emerging social media companies. The group is leveraging their collective experience and capital to identify and support startups developing the next generation of social platforms and related technologies.

This coordinated effort represents veteran investors from a major social platform working to influence the future direction of the social media industry.

hero.headline: Spurs upset Thunder in Game 7 to reach NBA Finals
hero.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday night, earning their spot in the NBA Finals against the New York Knicks.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs to victory with 22 points and seven rebounds, earning series MVP honors. The 7-foot-4 French star was emotional after the win, reflecting on achieving a childhood dream. "Realizing that some part of a childhood dream is going to come true," Wembanyama said. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it."

However, the victory was far from a one-man effort. Julian Champagnie scored 20 points and connected on six three-pointers for San Antonio. Dylan Harper made an impact off the bench while backup center Luke Kornet delivered a crucial block in the fourth quarter as the Thunder mounted a comeback attempt. After the game, Champagnie highlighted his team's star player, saying "We never knew if we were going to get this far but when you've got the greatest player in the world things happen."

The Thunder fought hard throughout the contest despite playing without Jalen Williams due to a hamstring injury. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP, was brilliant for Oklahoma City with 35 points and nine assists. However, no other Thunder teammate scored more than 20 points as they surrendered their championship title.

The Spurs sealed the series with a breakaway dunk in the final moments, ending any comeback hopes for the defending champions. Coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the defeat while looking forward for his team. "You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," Daigneault said. "And it's the NBA there are tough ones. We can also be really disappointed. There's nobody that we don't think we can beat, respectfully."

San Antonio will face the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio. History favors the Spurs in this matchup. The last time these franchises met in the Finals was in 1999, when San Antonio won the series 4-1.

The Spurs' run to the Finals represents a significant upset, as they were not expected to dethrone Oklahoma City. San Antonio combined strong defensive play with timely offensive execution throughout the series, extending the Western Conference Finals to the maximum seven games before capturing the deciding victory at home.

cards.headline: Dennis Hull, five-time NHL All-Star, dies at 81
cards.teaser: The former Chicago Blackhawks forward and 1972 Summit Series winner passed away.
cards.body:
Dennis Hull, a five-time NHL All-Star forward, died Saturday at age 81. He played alongside his brother Bobby Hull with the Chicago Blackhawks throughout his professional career.

Hull was celebrated as a skilled two-way player who made significant contributions on both offense and defense. He represented Canada in the 1972 Summit Series, helping the nation secure victory against the Soviet Union in a historic matchup.

cards.headline: Claude Lemieux's brain donated for CTE research
cards.teaser: The former NHL player's family will donate his brain to study repetitive brain injuries.
cards.body:
Claude Lemieux's brain is being donated to the Boston University CTE Center, his family announced Saturday. The contribution will support research into chronic traumatic encephalopathy and other neurological conditions resulting from head trauma.

The Boston University CTE Center focuses on understanding the long-term effects of repetitive brain injuries. Lemieux's family decided to participate in this ongoing research effort.

cards.headline: PSG beats Arsenal in shootout to win second straight Champions League title
cards.teaser: Paris Saint-Germain became only the second team to win consecutive Champions League titles.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain won the Champions League title by defeating Arsenal on penalties in a dramatic final held in Budapest, Hungary. The match went to a shootout, with PSG ultimately prevailing in the penalty phase.

The victory marks PSG's second consecutive Champions League title, making them only the second team in the competition's history to achieve back-to-back wins.

cards.headline: Fernando Tatis Jr. ends homer drought with 451-foot blast
cards.teaser: The Padres star hit his first home run of the season against the Nationals.
cards.body:
Fernando Tatis Jr. finally broke through with his first home run of the season, launching a 451-foot solo shot to left field against the Nationals. The Padres outfielder had been dealing with an MLB-worst home run drought heading into the game.

The mammoth blast ended an extended stretch without a homer for Tatis, who had been searching for power at the plate early in the season.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark held to six points in Fever loss
cards.teaser: The Indiana star struggled offensively in a defeat to the Fire.
cards.body:
Caitlin Clark scored just six points as the Indiana Fever lost to the Chicago Fire 100-84 on Saturday night. The star guard struggled to find her offensive rhythm in the game.

Clark's performance fell well short of her usual scoring output for Indiana, marking an uncharacteristic night for one of the team's top scorers.

cards.headline: Tennessee coach Karen Weekly denies handshake line accusation
cards.teaser: The Volunteers softball coach called a player's claim a lie after their NCAA tournament game.
cards.body:
Tennessee softball coach Karen Weekly denied an accusation from Texas Tech third baseman Taylor Pannell following the Volunteers' 2-1 extra-inning victory at the Women's College World Series on Saturday. Pannell alleged that Weekly told her during the postgame handshake line that she made a mistake transferring from Tennessee.

Weekly called the accusation a lie. Pannell had previously played for the Volunteers before transferring to Texas Tech.

hero.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remaining 2026 Tour Dates Citing Health Concerns
hero.body:
The 92-year-old music legend Frankie Valli has announced the cancellation of all remaining 2026 dates on what was marketed as a farewell tour with the Four Seasons. In a statement, Valli expressed his regret to fans while explaining his need to prioritize his health.

"So sorry to disappoint," Valli said in his announcement, directing his message to ticket holders who had purchased seats for the canceled shows. The decision affects the complete schedule of performances originally planned for the remainder of the year.

The Four Seasons, which Valli has led since the early 1960s, became one of the most influential vocal groups in popular music history. The group's catalog includes enduring hits such as "Sherry," "Big Girls Don't Cry," "Walk Like a Man," and "Can't Take My Eyes Off You." Their legacy extended beyond music when their story was adapted into the acclaimed Broadway musical "Jersey Boys."

Throughout his career, Valli maintained a reputation for his distinctive vocal abilities, particularly his remarkable falsetto. The group achieved further recognition when they were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1990. Despite his age, Valli had continued performing regularly on tour until this recent health-related decision.

The announcement did not include details about any specific health condition affecting the singer. Valli's statement focused solely on the need to cancel 2026 dates to concentrate on his health, without clarifying whether these cancellations might be permanent or if he could potentially return to performing in subsequent years.

Fans who purchased tickets for the canceled shows will need to contact their original point of purchase to seek refunds. While individual venues and ticketing platforms have not yet announced a unified refund process, standard procedures typically apply to cancellations made for health reasons.

This development represents a notable moment for the extensive fan base that has followed Valli's six-decade career in the music industry. His vocal talents made him one of the most recognizable performers in American popular music history. The Four Seasons' influence on pop and rock music remains significant decades after their peak years of commercial success.

The farewell tour had been positioned as a final chance for supporters to experience the legendary performer in concert, making the cancellation a significant disappointment for those who had planned to attend. The decision underscores the physical demands of touring at an advanced age, even for artists with remarkable longevity in their careers.

cards.headline: Search Suspended for Man Believed to Be Alaskan Bush People Star Matt Brown
cards.teaser: Authorities have suspended the search for a man believed to be reality TV personality Matt Brown after reports suggested he took his own life.
cards.body:
The search for a man believed to be Matt Brown from the Discovery Channel series "Alaskan Bush People" has been suspended. Brown's brother Bear said Matt was spotted near a river where police say a man went missing.

Authorities reported that a man went missing in the area, and family members have expressed concern that Brown is likely dead. The 42-year-old reality star appeared on the show alongside his family, who lived off the grid in Alaska and later Washington state. Brown had been public about his struggles in recent years.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Cast Member Over Use of Racial Slur for Second Consecutive Year
cards.teaser: Peacock has dismissed Vasana Montgomery from the upcoming season of Love Island USA after social media posts surfaced showing use of a racial slur.
cards.body:
Love Island USA has removed cast member Vasana Montgomery from the show before the season premiere after social media posts emerged showing her using the n-word. Montgomery will not appear when the reality dating series returns to Peacock on June 2.

This marks the second consecutive year the show has dismissed a contestant over similar social media posts. The pattern has raised questions about the casting process and background checks for reality television participants. The show had not yet begun airing when the decision was made.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Flips Piano During Denver Performance
cards.teaser: The country music star overturned a piano onstage while performing "Sand in My Boots" in Denver.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen flipped over a piano during a performance in Denver. The country star appeared upset with the instrument while performing his song "Sand in My Boots" onstage.

Wallen's action during the concert drew comparisons to Billy Joel, who famously destroyed pianos during performances earlier in his career. Video of the incident circulated on social media following the show.

cards.headline: Warner Bros. Pictures Chief Warns Against Cutting Development Budgets
cards.teaser: Michael De Luca cautioned that reducing funds for original material could dry up the creative pipeline for studios.
cards.body:
Warner Bros. Pictures chief Michael De Luca cautioned industry leaders against making drastic cuts to development budgets during a session at the Produced By conference, hosted by the Producers Guild of America. He warned that slashing investment in original material too severely risks depleting the creative pipeline.

De Luca emphasized that consistently identifying new talent and fresh creative voices should be a core priority for studio executives. He presented his remarks as a master class on studio leadership, underscoring how the ongoing search for emerging creators is vital to maintaining a healthy pipeline of content.

cards.headline: Niall Horan Reflects on Liam Payne's Death Two Years Later
cards.teaser: The former One Direction member discussed his late bandmate's 2024 death in a new interview, describing both sadness and fond memories.
cards.body:
Niall Horan discussed his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne's passing in an interview with The Times of London. Payne died in 2024 at age 31 after falling from a hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Horan reflected on their shared history, noting that memories of Payne bring both sadness and moments of laughter. The two performers were part of One Direction, the hugely successful boy band that dominated the 2010s.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Open to Mentoring Next Spider-Man Actor
cards.teaser: The current Spider-Man star said he would like to help set up the next chapter for whoever takes over the Marvel franchise.
cards.body:
Tom Holland told Empire magazine he's excited about passing the Spider-Man role to the next actor in the franchise. He hopes to mentor whoever takes on the part next, similar to how Robert Downey Jr. guided him when he joined the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

Holland is open to being involved in establishing the next chapter of the character, whether that's Miles Morales, Spider-Gwen, Spider-Woman, or another variant. He has played Peter Parker across multiple Marvel films since joining the MCU.

hero.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by US envoys
hero.body:
President Trump has asked for amendments to a tentative agreement that his envoys negotiated with Iranian counterparts, according to senior administration officials and sources briefed on the matter.

During a Friday Situation Room meeting, Trump indicated he wants to finalize the deal but is seeking to strengthen certain provisions he considers important, particularly those addressing Iran's nuclear material. The requested changes have triggered another round of negotiations between the parties that officials say could extend several days.

The tentative agreement, which both sides reached earlier this week, would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz if both the United States and Iran approve it. Trump stated he will only sign a deal "where we get everything we want," according to reports from his conversations with media outlets.

Trump made a public announcement on Friday that an agreement has been "largely negotiated" after calls with leaders from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Turkey and Israel. He indicated that "final aspects and details" of the deal were still being discussed and would be announced shortly.

However, Iran's state-aligned news agency contested Trump's characterization, stating that his assertion about the deal being nearly final was "inconsistent with reality." The agency also reported that Iran insists the Strait of Hormuz would remain under Iranian control, including determining passage routes, timing and methods.

According to details reported by international media outlets, the proposed agreement would include opening the strait with no tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension. Iran would be permitted to freely sell oil while negotiations occur on its nuclear program. The United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports in return.

Additional reported provisions include an official declaration ending the war, negotiations on Iran's nuclear program within 30 to 60 days, and potentially releasing approximately 25 billion dollars in frozen Iranian assets.

Trump convened meetings with his negotiating team, including special envoy Steve Witkoff, adviser Jared Kushner, and Vice President JD Vance to discuss the latest proposals.

The potential deal has generated strong reactions from Republican hawks who have long advocated for military action against Iran. Former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo criticized the rumored terms, claiming they resembled the approach taken by the Obama administration in the 2015 nuclear agreement that Trump withdrew from in 2018.

However, some officials involved in previous negotiations suggested the deal could still represent progress toward peace. The timing for a final agreement remains uncertain, though Trump has expressed his desire to complete negotiations quickly.

cards.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks in next 48 hours
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch a major attack within the next two days based on intelligence from US and European allies.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is bracing for a major attack from Russia expected within the next 48 hours, based on intelligence shared by the U.S. and European allies. He anticipates the attacks will occur at night in the coming days.

The Ukrainian government is preparing for what it expects will be significant military action from Russian forces.

cards.headline: Justice Department seeks judge's recusal from Georgia election case
cards.teaser: The Justice Department asked a federal judge to step aside from a lawsuit against Georgia election officials, citing her attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis.
cards.body:
The Justice Department filed a motion asking a federal judge to recuse herself from overseeing the department's lawsuit against Georgia election officials. The request argues that her attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis raises questions about her ability to remain impartial.

The filing was submitted to the US District Court. The department contends that the judge's participation in the Willis event creates an appearance of bias that warrants her removal from the case.

cards.headline: UN blacklists Israeli and Russian forces for sexual violence during conflict
cards.teaser: The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces to its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict, including allegations of rape against detained Palestinians.
cards.body:
The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces for the first time to its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict. The inclusion covers allegations of rape against detained Palestinians by Israeli forces.

The report released lists 77 government and non-government parties in countries credibly suspected of patterns of rape or other forms of sexual violence during armed conflict. This marks the first time either Israeli or Russian forces have appeared on the list.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor withdraws from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly threatening President Trump has stepped down from the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped down from the case, according to a recent court filing. Comey was indicted for allegedly threatening the life of President Trump in a since-deleted social media post of seashells.

A notice of substitution filed in the Eastern District of North Carolina stated that Matthew, the lead prosecutor, is withdrawing from the case. The filing provides no explanation for the prosecutor's decision to step away.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor deploys state police to ICE facility protests
cards.teaser: New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill deployed state police to maintain order outside a Newark immigration detention center following escalating protests.
cards.body:
State police have been stationed outside the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark as protests continue at the facility. A hunger and labor strike by detained immigrants demanding better conditions and medical care entered its ninth day on Saturday.

The deployment has created a buffer between opposing groups. Pro-immigrant protesters and Trump-supporting counterprotesters demonstrated outside the facility, separated by barricades set up by state police. Both groups vocalized their positions across the barriers as tensions remained high.

cards.headline: Judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: A judge agreed to review President Trump's $1.8 billion fund that has sparked backlash and exposed divisions within the Republican Party.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Miami has reopened President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service to examine a $1.8 billion settlement. The settlement, which Trump reached with the Justice Department, is being scrutinized following a third-party motion claiming it "is a product of collusion and is itself a fraud on the court."

The original lawsuit was brought by Trump and his sons after their personal and business tax returns were leaked by a former IRS contractor. The fund has sparked significant backlash since its announcement, creating divisions within the Republican Party.
